title: Team USA takes down France for fifth consecutive World Cup gold medal
content:
Team USA continued its reign as the most dominant squad in women’s basketball, claiming its fifth consecutive FIBA World Cup gold medal, with Sunday’s assertive 97-79 win over France.

Despite fan and media skepticism that the Americans had met their match with the motivated French, who had dominated the tournament up until the championship game, Team USA proved its dynasty is in good hands. But the highly anticipated rematch of the 2024 Olympic gold medal game was not a seamless victory for the United States.

For the first 20 minutes, France made sure the U.S. felt it everywhere on the court. On defense, its overwhelming ball pressure and disruption it created getting into passing lanes prevented Team USA from establishing any offensive rhythm. Offensively, it unloaded an unrelenting downpour from 3-point range.

After an 11-0 run by France put the Les Bleues ahead by 14 points to start the second quarter, Team USA responded with a 10-2 run of its own, sparked by a short-range jumper from Breanna Stewart off the give-and-go action with Jackie Young.

Young was Team USA’s leading scorer coming into the game, averaging 11.2 points per game throughout the tournament. But it was Stewart, who was named tournament MVP, acting as a steadying force throughout. She finished with a game-high 22 points and 10 rebounds en route to her fourth World Cup gold medal, joining Sue Bird with the most of any player in tournament history.

Five U.S. players finished scoring in double figures. Young added 18 points, five rebounds and five assists, while Chelsea Gray added 14 points, Kahleah Copper 13 points, and Caitlin Clark 12 points off the bench.

France came into Sunday’s gold medal game beating its opponents by an average of 35.6 points. The French remained the aggressors through the first half, but looked shell-shocked when the U.S. flipped the script to start the third quarter.

Team USA came out of the break with a ferocity that was absent through the first two quarters.

Stewart used a screen from Gray to get downhill for a clean look at the rim, tying the game with a layup to start the second half. On the next play, Collier put the U.S. ahead with a backdoor layup off the assist from Young. Before the quarter was over, the U.S. held a 16-point lead, which it extended to as many as 19 points in the fourth quarter.

France’s largest deficit of the tournament before Sunday’s game was 7 points against Korea. Dominique Malonga led France with 21 points and seven rebounds, and Gabby Williams added 20 points. She was held scoreless in the third quarter, failing to score until under the two-minute mark in the fourth quarter.

The next World Cup will be played in Tokyo in 2030 with a changed window, running from Nov. 26 to Dec. 8. The schedule change means there will be no overlap with the WNBA schedule as the league’s footprint continues to expand.
